Figures of different shapes, each opened on its own, and the `fit` option. All
are png. Other formats are on [image formats](e-formats.html), and the same
shapes in galleries and layouts are on [wide figures in
galleries](i-wide-galleries.html).

With `fit: auto`, the default, a figure opens by its shape:

  | Figure                                                                                           | Opens                                     |
  | ---                                                                                              | ---                                       |
  | Most images, photos and plots, portrait or landscape                                             | whole, never larger than its real size    |
  | Wide strip: at least 3 times wider than tall, and under a quarter of the screen tall when whole  | at screen height, at the spot you clicked |
  | Tall strip: at least 3 times taller than wide, and under a quarter of the screen wide when whole | at screen width, from the top             |

`fit: contain`, `height`, or `width` sets this for one figure. A small image
opens at its own size, and scrolling still zooms it in, up to `max-zoom`.

Where you click a strip on the page is its focal point. Click panel 12 of a
20-panel collage, and the viewer opens with panel 12 in the middle of the
screen, or flush with the end near either end. The 0 key and double-click return
to it. Opened from the keyboard, a strip starts at its left end or top. Zooming
out still shows the whole figure.

Shift+scroll, or a sideways trackpad swipe, pans along a collage sideways and
along a tall strip up and down. Zoomed in both ways, it pans sideways.

The plots are drawn with these helpers:

```{r}
# A collage: `n` panels side by side, like a wide patchwork figure.
collage <- function(n = 12) {
  set.seed(1)
  par(mfrow = c(1, n), mar = c(3, 3, 2, 1))
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    plot(
      cumsum(rnorm(200)),
      type = "l",
      main = paste("Panel", i),
      xlab = "",
      ylab = "",
      col = hcl.colors(n)[i],
      lwd = 2
    )
  }
}

# A tall strip: `n` rows stacked, like a tall patchwork figure.
# Each seed gets its own palette (without its lightest end), so different
# strips look different.
strip <- function(seed = 2, n = 8) {
  set.seed(seed)
  palette <- c(
    "Viridis",
    "Plasma",
    "Zissou 1",
    "Dark 3",
    "Sunset",
    "Cividis",
    "Dynamic",
    "Inferno"
  )[(seed - 2) %% 8 + 1]
  par(mfrow = c(n, 1), mar = c(2, 3, 2, 1))
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    plot(
      cumsum(rnorm(100)),
      type = "l",
      main = paste0("Strip ", seed, ", row ", i),
      xlab = "",
      ylab = "",
      col = hcl.colors(n + 2, palette)[i],
      lwd = 2
    )
  }
}

wave <- function(k = 1) {
  x <- seq(0, 4 * pi, length.out = 400)
  col <- hcl.colors(4, "Dark 3")[k]
  plot(
    x,
    sin(k * x),
    type = "n",
    main = paste("Wave", k),
    xlab = "x",
    ylab = "sin(kx)"
  )
  polygon(
    c(x, rev(x)),
    c(sin(k * x), rep(0, length(x))),
    col = adjustcolor(col, 0.35),
    border = NA
  )
  lines(x, sin(k * x), lwd = 2, col = col)
}
```

## Wide collage {#c1 expect-fit="height" shift-scroll="x"}

A 25 × 2 inch collage. It opens in panzoom at screen height, and Shift+scroll
moves sideways.

```{r}
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   A row of 12 small line plots of random walks, each in its own color
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 25
#| fig-height: 2
#| fig-cap: "A 25 × 2 inch collage of 12 random walks, as png."

collage(n = 12)
```

## Whole figure {#c2 expect-fit="contain" shift-scroll="none"}

The collage from [case 1](#c1) with `fit: contain`. It opens whole, as a thin
strip.

```{r}
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   A row of 12 small line plots of random walks, each in its own color
#| panzoom:
#|   fit: contain
#| fig-width: 25
#| fig-height: 2
#| fig-cap: "A 25 × 2 inch collage of 12 random walks."

collage(n = 12)
```

## Moderately wide figure {#c3 expect-fit="contain"}

A 16 × 4 inch figure, wide but readable whole. It isn't a strip, so it opens
whole.

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "A row of 4 small line plots of random walks, each in its own color"
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: "A 16 × 4 inch collage of 4 random walks."

collage(n = 4)
```

## Tall strip {#c4 expect-fit="width" shift-scroll="y"}

A 4 × 15 inch strip. It opens at screen width from its top, and Shift+scroll
moves up and down.

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "A column of 8 small line plots of random walks"
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 15
#| fig-cap: "A 4 × 15 inch strip of 8 random walks."

strip(seed = 2, n = 8)
```

## Large poster {#c5 expect-fit="contain" shift-scroll="zoomed-x"}

A 24 × 18 inch poster. It opens whole. Zoomed in, it extends past the screen
both ways, and Shift+scroll moves sideways.

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "A grid of 48 small line plots of random walks, in 6 rows of 8"
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 24
#| fig-height: 18
#| fig-cap: "A 24 × 18 inch poster of 48 random walks."

set.seed(3)
par(mfrow = c(6, 8), mar = c(2, 2, 2, 1))
for (i in 1:48) {
  plot(
    cumsum(rnorm(100)),
    type = "l",
    main = paste("Panel", i),
    xlab = "",
    ylab = ""
  )
}
```

## Portrait photo {#c6 expect-fit="contain"}

A 9:16 portrait photo. It isn't a strip, so it opens whole on any screen width.

```markdown {.show-source}
![A sailboat off Edgartown, Martha's Vineyard.](../../images/mv-4.jpg){.panzoom width=30% fig-alt="A sailboat with a flag-striped sail off a sandy beach"}
```

## Small plot {#c7 expect-fit="contain" expect-scale="1"}

A 288 × 192 px plot. It opens at its real size, centered, instead of enlarged to
fill the screen, and scrolling still zooms in, up to `max-zoom`.

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "Scatter plot of vapor pressure rising steeply with temperature"
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 3
#| fig-height: 2
#| fig-dpi: 48
#| fig-cap: "Vapor pressure of mercury against temperature."

plot(pressure)
```

## Fit to height {#c8 expect-open="panzoom" expect-fit="height" expect-zoom-out="no"}

An ordinary plot with `fit: height`. On a screen wider than the plot (1.4:1),
filling the height already shows the whole plot, so it opens like `fit: contain`
and can't zoom out. [Case 10](#c10) shows `fit: height` where it makes a
difference.

```{r}
#| panzoom:
#|   fit: height
#| fig-alt: "Plot titled Wave 3: a sine curve with its area to the axis shaded"

wave(k = 3)
```

## Fit to width {#c9 expect-open="panzoom" expect-fit="width" expect-zoom-out="yes"}

An ordinary plot with `fit: width`. Filling the width makes the plot taller than
the screen, so it opens closer than the whole plot and zooms out to it.

```{r}
#| panzoom:
#|   fit: width
#| fig-alt: "Plot titled Wave 4: a sine curve with its area to the axis shaded"

wave(k = 4)
```

## Fit to height on a wide figure {#c10 expect-open="panzoom" expect-fit="height" expect-zoom-out="yes"}

A 12 × 4.5 inch figure with `fit: height`. It isn't a strip, since shown whole
it is over a quarter of the screen tall, so `fit: auto` would open it whole.
With `fit: height`, it opens filling the screen height, up to its real size, at
the spot you clicked, and zooms out to the whole figure.

```{r}
#| panzoom:
#|   fit: height
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-alt: "A row of 6 small line plots of random walks, each in its own color"

collage(n = 6)
```

## Long caption and description {#c11 expect-open="panzoom" expect-fit="height" expect-zoom-out="yes"}

The figure from [case 10](#c10) with a long caption and description.
`fit: height` fills the height left above them, so it opens smaller than case
10. The caption scrolls past a quarter of the screen and the description past a
fifth, so the image keeps about half.

```{r}
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   A row of 6 small line plots of random walks, each in its own color
#| panzoom:
#|   fit: height
#|   description: >-
#|     A long description, to take room below the image. Each panel is a random
#|     walk of 200 steps, drawn with `plot()` from base R in a one-row layout
#|     (`par(mfrow = c(1, 6))`), colored along the `hcl.colors()` palette. The
#|     figure is 12 by 4.5 inches, which knitr writes at 192 dpi (2304 by 864
#|     px). With `fit: height` the viewer opens it as tall as the space above
#|     this text allows, and no taller than its real size. Drag or use the arrow
#|     keys to move along the figure, scroll or press the minus key to zoom out
#|     to the whole of it, and press 0 to come back to this opening view.
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Six random walks side by side, opened with `fit: height` under a long
#|   description.
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 4.5

collage(n = 6)
```
